items.title: Keeping culture alive in a remote company
items.prompt: Your class has attended a panel discussion on how organisations can keep a strong culture when many staff work remotely. You made the notes below. Write an essay discussing two of the methods in your notes. Explain which method is more effective, giving reasons to support your opinion.
points: Methods: regular in-person events · clear written communication norms · mentoring schemes
Opinions: “People need to meet face to face.” · “Culture is what you write down and repeat.” · “New staff learn culture from people, not handbooks.”

items.title: Getting cars out of city centres
items.prompt: Your class has discussed how cities could reduce traffic in their centres. Write an essay discussing two of the methods in your notes. Explain which method would be more effective, giving reasons.
points: Methods: congestion charges · cheaper, more frequent public transport · car-free zones
Opinions: “Only a charge changes behaviour.” · “People will leave the car if the bus is better.” · “Car-free zones kill local shops.”

items.title: Lifelong learning at work
items.prompt: You have attended a talk on how employers can encourage staff to keep learning throughout their careers. Write an essay discussing two of the methods in your notes and explain which is more effective.
points: Methods: funded external courses · paid time off for study · internal knowledge-sharing sessions
Opinions: “Courses are expensive and quickly forgotten.” · “Without time, nobody studies.” · “Colleagues are the best teachers.”

items.title: Better communication with foreign distributors
items.prompt: Your manager has asked for proposals on improving communication between your company and its foreign distributors. Write a proposal describing the current problems, suggesting two improvements and explaining how they would benefit the business.

items.title: Trade fair visit: lessons learnt
items.prompt: You recently organised a three-day trade fair visit for your sales team. Write a report for your director evaluating what went well and what went less well, and recommending changes for next year.

items.title: A resource that changed how you work
items.prompt: A business magazine has invited readers to review a book, podcast or online course that helped them professionally. Describe it, explain what you learnt from it and say who would benefit from it most.

items.title: Answering a customer complaint
items.prompt: A key customer has complained that a delivery arrived late and partly damaged. Write a letter to the customer apologising, explaining what went wrong and setting out what you will do to put things right and prevent it happening again.

items.title: Doing business in the Czech Republic
items.prompt: An international colleague has asked for your advice before their first business trip to the Czech Republic. Write an email explaining what they should know about meetings, negotiations and building relationships.

items.title: Reducing our environmental impact
items.prompt: Your company wants to reduce its environmental impact. Write a proposal suggesting two practical changes, outlining their costs and explaining the benefits you expect.

items.title: Staff survey on working hours
items.prompt: Write a report for the board on the results of a staff survey about working hours. Summarise the main findings and make recommendations.
points: 48% feel pressure to answer emails in the evening
30% would accept a four-day week with longer days
